title: candidate-debrief-ryan-murphy-2026-02-28-draft
content:
Quick personal debrief / scratchpad after candidate loop. Still rough—want to capture gut + concrete examples before forgetting. Will move to structured scorecard later.

Candidate: Ryan Murphy
Role: Research Engineer, Inference (RD/ML-Infra)
Interview date: 2026-02-27 (loop: system-design, coding, infra deep-dive, manager)
Interviewer(s): Priya P., Jordan L., Alex Z. (takeaways)
Resume notes: strong distributed systems background (previous at scale-up focused on model serving), solid Py/C++ experience. Has open-source contribs around tokenizer optimizations.

Round-by-round notes:
- Coding (Priya): medium-hard exercise on streaming parser + backpressure. Ryan implemented baseline quickly, clear thought in incremental improvements. Left some edge-case error handling undone but noted tradeoffs. Time management good. Uses tests to validate.
  - Example: suggested using generator-based streaming pipeline to reduce memory, then added small bounded buffer with backpressure signals.
  - Concern: relied on single-threaded async model; when asked about multi-gpu batching, answers were high-level but not concrete.

- System design (Jordan): designed an inference prefetcher + KV-cache eviction policy for variable-length sequences across mixed batch sizes. Good grasp of latency vs throughput tradeoffs. Proposed per-customer cache namespaces and lightweight TTL heuristics.
  - Strength: thought through quota isolation and simple fallbacks.
  - Weakness: didn't quantify memory/perf tradeoffs or propose specific eviction algorithm beyond LRU+size threshold. Could probe more on kernel-level risks.

- Infra deep-dive (Alex): dug into experience with deployment, CI for model builds, quantization toolchain. Ryan has hands-on with ONNX/quant config, some experience with custom CUDA kernels but not full kernel dev. Familiar with K8s CRDs and sidecar patterns for model metrics.
  - Example: described rollout strategy with shadowing then canary, metrics gating on p99 latency and token-quality evals. Good operational instincts.
  - Concern: limited production debugging experience on multi-tenant GPU pools (mostly single-tenant at prior company).

- Manager loop: good culture fit, communication clear, asks good questions about long-term roadmap (model catalog, private deployments). Expressed desire to own a horizontal infra piece.

Scorecard (1-5, subjective):
- Technical/coding: 4
- System design (inference): 4
- Low-level kernel/dev (CUDA/core kernel): 3
- Production debugging / multi-tenant infra: 3
- Culture/team fit: 4
- Communication: 5

Summary / recommendation (draft): Strong candidate for mid-senior Research Engineer role focused on serving/runtime and infra. Has the right instincts for production inference and a practical approach to rollouts and caching. Gaps: deep kernel development and explicit multi-tenant GPU debugging experience. Recommendation: move to take-home or final hiring committee with hire-for-IC role (level: Senior Engineer) but pair with planned onboarding focusing on kernel/quantization deep dives.

Probing questions / follow-ups to verify before offer:
- Ask for a concrete example where they diagnosed a GPU OOM in a multi-tenant environment and what metrics/logs they used.
- Ask for a short write-up of a cache eviction strategy with cost/latency estimates (simple calc).
- Sample code review: request small kernel-adjacent change or profiling output they produced previously.

Action items (personal):
- Move notes into standard scorecard template and add numeric rubric items (by 2026-03-02).
- Send follow-up request for write-up + traces (assigned to Alex).
- Sync with Talent Partner to schedule take-home (if committee ok)

Misc notes / mental model:
- Good hire if we need someone who can own product-facing inference features quickly and collaborate with ML/research teams.
- Might not be best pick if primary need is deep CUDA kernel lead; consider for two-hire plan (one infra/product-facing, one kernel specialist).

Raw verbatim quotes I want to remember:
- "I usually shadow new models in prod with a shadow traffic window for at least 48 hours and then only enable canary after stable p99 for 2 windows."
- "Quant perf regressions are mostly about IO and kernel choice; I prefer to start with profiling to see if tokenization or KV cache is the real culprit."

End of quick scratchpad. Will formalize and share with loopers.
